theme_central: Oaths by the winds and cosmic phenomena to establish the certainty of the Judgment, illustrated by the fate of the ancient peoples who rejected their messengers.
sources_note: 3-part structure precisely sourced (literary analysis by Angelika Neuwirth via grokipedia): 1-23, 24-46, 47-60. Narrative of Ibrahim's guests detailed (24-30).

branches.title: Oaths, promise of the Judgment
branches.resume: Oaths by the scattering winds, certain and inescapable promise of the Judgment.

children.t: Oaths by the winds, certain promise of the Judgment

branches.title: Paradise of the pious, signs
branches.resume: Description of Paradise for the pious, signs in creation and within man himself.

children.t: Description of Paradise for the pious, sleeping little at night, seeking forgiveness at dawn
Signs on earth and within man himself

branches.title: Ibrahim's guests, destruction of Lot's people
branches.resume: The angels visiting Ibrahim, announcement of Ishaq; destruction of Lot's people.

children.t: Ibrahim's guests (the angels), announcement of Ishaq's birth
Destruction of Lot's people, except the believers

branches.title: Musa, 'Ad, Thamud, Nuh
branches.resume: Brief reminder of Musa/Pharaoh, 'Ad destroyed by the wind, Thamud by the Cry, the people of Nuh.

children.t: 'Ad destroyed by the wind, Thamud by the Cry, the people of Nuh

branches.title: Signs of creation
branches.resume: The sky expanded, the earth spread out, everything created in pairs; fleeing toward Allah.

children.t: The expanded sky, everything created in pairs, fleeing toward Allah

branches.title: Messengers called liars
branches.resume: Every messenger called a sorcerer or a madman; jinn and men created only to worship Allah alone.

children.t: Every messenger called a sorcerer or a madman by his people
Jinn and men created only to worship Allah alone; He is the Provider
